title: meilynx.witness_manifest.v1
description: The index of a witness file (anchor file): the chain heads a gateway reported to its control plane, which the control plane kept append-only, for one gateway. The file is a ZIP archive (or the same tree as a directory) holding witness-manifest.json at its root, each anchor statement at anchors/<chain>/<seq:020d>.json, each timestamp token at anchors/<chain>/<seq:020d>.<tsa_id>.tsr and each head the gateway signed at head-signatures/<chain>/<head_sequence:020d>.json. witness-manifest.json is written as RFC 8785 (JCS) bytes. Content-free: chain names, sequences, head hashes, gateway, organization and project ids, times, digests and signatures. A head with basis `timestamp` counts on its own when one of its tokens verifies over a canonical meilynx.anchor.v1 statement that names this chain at this sequence with this event_hash and whose run_id names this proxy_id (`<proxy_id>/<boot id>`). A head with basis `reported` (and a timestamp head whose statement names no gateway) counts only when the manifest is signed and the signature verifies under the project's evidence attestation key the reader pins. Signature: ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 over the bytes "meilynx.witness_manifest.v1" 0x00 followed by the RFC 8785 bytes of the manifest without its `signature` member; `value` is the 64-byte r || s in standard base64; `key_id` is the RFC 7638 thumbprint of the attestation key. The record is tamper-evident against the witnessed heads; a witnessed head shows that the head was reported at that time, not that the records behind it were kept.

generated_at.description: When the control plane built the file (its own clock).

proxy_id.description: The gateway the file witnesses. Printable ASCII without '/', so it is the run_id prefix of its anchor statements. The verifier refuses (exit 2) a pack labelled with another gateway.

chains.description: Sorted by chain name (ordinal), each chain once.

omitted_chains.description: Chains with witnessed heads left out by the file's cap (the least recently witnessed).

contradictions.description: Integrity findings the control plane recorded for this gateway (newest first, capped): a fork (another hash at a sequence already reported), a rewind (a lower sequence after a higher one) or a witness conflict (another payload under a held key). Both contradicting heads are listed under `chains`, so a pack can match at most one of them.

key_id.description: RFC 7638 thumbprint of the project's evidence attestation key; null when unsigned.

reason.description: `no_attestation_key`: the control plane that built the file has no evidence attestation key configured, so only timestamp-backed heads count.

disclosure.description: Fixed text: what the file shows and does not show, and, for an unsigned file, that reported heads do not count.

gen_time.description: The token's genTime, to the second, as the control plane read it when it verified the token on arrival.

heads.description: Sorted by seq, then basis (`reported` before `timestamp`), then event_hash. Capped to the newest heads by sequence.

omitted_earlier_heads.description: Heads of this chain at lower sequences left out by the cap.

received_at.description: When the control plane first received a token for this head.

statement.description: anchors/<chain>/<seq:020d>.json, the exact meilynx.anchor.v1 statement bytes the tokens are over.

tokens.description: By tsa_id. Only tokens the control plane verified on arrival are listed.

observed_at.description: The gateway's clock when it read the head (its heartbeat snapshot).

received_at.description: The control plane's clock when it received the report: the witnessed time.

signed_head.description: head-signatures/<chain>/<seq:020d>.json: {statement, signature}, the meilynx.evidence.chain_head.v1 statement the gateway signed with its evidence key (meilynx-verify SPEC §12) naming this proxy_id, chain, seq and event_hash, as relayed on the heartbeat. Checked under the pack's evidence keys when the reader pins them; it never makes a head count on its own.
